steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Classical Hollywood narrative is the dominant storytelling model in US cinema, characterised by cause-and-effect logic, goal-oriented protagonists, narrative closure and invisible filmmaking style. | Key Fact: The three-act structure divides the narrative into setup (establishing characters and conflict), confrontation (complications and obstacles) and resolution (climax and closure). | Key Fact: Cause-and-effect logic means that events in the narrative are driven by character decisions and actions rather than coincidence, creating a sense of narrative necessity and coherence. | Key Fact: The protagonist in classical Hollywood is typically an active, goal-driven individual whose desires define the narrative trajectory and whose actions propel the plot forward.
